description: Given a tree of n nodes labeled 0 to n-1 and n-1 edges, find all root nodes that produce minimum height trees. Return a list of their labels.
intuition: The center of a tree minimizes the maximum distance to any node. Find it by repeatedly trimming leaves from the outside in. The last 1 or 2 nodes remaining are the centers — the optimal roots.
approach: Repeatedly remove leaf nodes (degree 1) from the outside in. The last remaining 1 or 2 nodes are the roots of minimum height trees (the centers of the tree).

explanation:
1. Find all initial leaf nodes (degree 1).
2. Remove leaves layer by layer, updating neighbor degrees. Finish the entire current layer before checking the while condition again.
3. When a neighbor becomes a leaf (degree 1), add it to the next layer.
4. Stop when 1 or 2 nodes remain — they are the centers.
hints: The root of a minimum height tree is a center of the tree.
A tree has one or two centers.
Repeatedly trim leaves until 1-2 nodes remain.

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: V = vertices; E = edges. The input is a tree, so E = V − 1.
timeComplexityBreakdown.note: A node becomes a leaf and is removed at most once. Across all layers, each removed leaf deletes one connection. Substitute E = V − 1 to get O(V).
